Subject: Request: evidence for misuse detection & notification (RFP follow-up)

Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team appreciated the walkthrough of routing and fallback behavior. As part of our security review for the RFP, the procurement and security teams asked for a focused evidence bundle around "misuse monitoring": specifically, examples of telemetry and alerting that show how Redwood detects high-risk automated abuse and how incidents are escalated.

Can you provide:
- Example alerts and signal thresholds (what triggers a severity-2 vs severity-1)
- Sample telemetry payloads / log snippets (anonymized) showing detection + KV cache/prefix indicators
- Typical detection-to-alert latency SLA for production workloads (p95/p99)
- Escalation matrix that shows who is notified and when (including cross-region failover)
- Retention windows for telemetry and audit logs (SOC 2 alignment)

We need these items by EOD Wednesday (Jan 21) to close the security review. If anything will take longer, please flag now.

Best,
Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform Security
SafeHarbor Bank

Alex — thanks, noted. Sending an initial package below and looping Rishi/Tessa for the narrower technical pieces.

What you'll find attached:
- misuse_monitoring_evidence.csv (sample anonymized telemetry rows with event type, model_id, score, flagged_rules)
- escalation_matrix.pdf (operational contacts, severity definitions, SLA targets)
- retention_policy_summary.docx (retention windows for logs, telemetry, and KV cache entries)

Quick summary answers up front:
- Threshold model: events are scored by ensemble signals (rate anomalies, content-policy model score, user-behavior heuristics). Severity-1 is reserved for active exploitation patterns (automated account takeover, large-scale prompt-injection across sessions). Severity-2 covers sustained suspicious activity that requires investigation.
- Detection-to-alert SLA: p95 = 18s, p99 = 42s for our hosted tier under typical load; Dedicated customers can configure tighter latency targets.
- Escalation: automatic alert -> on-call infra (15m escalation) -> security ops (30m) -> customer CISO contact (1h) depending on severity. Cross-region failover is handled by routing policies; the escalation_matrix.pdf shows regional contacts.

Rishi/Tessa, see Alex's asks. Alex — Rishi will attach the telemetry examples and a short note about anonymization strategy. Tessa will add details about sampling and retention.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: misuse_monitoring_evidence.csv (CSV, 12 rows), escalation_matrix.pdf (PDF, 3 pages), retention_policy_summary.docx (DOCX, 2 pages)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: evidence for misuse detection & notification (RFP follow-up)

Alex — following up with the technical snippets you asked for. I've attached three anonymized examples in the CSV. Below are clarifications & implementation notes.

1) Telemetry payload examples (in misuse_monitoring_evidence.csv): each row is pseudonymized and includes: timestamp, region, model_variant, user_bucket_id (hashed), event_type, ensemble_score, rule_match_tags, kv_cache_hit (boolean), prefix_similarity_score. These are representative rows only; production telemetry emits rich context (token counts, latency_ms, batching_id).

2) Detection signals and thresholds:
- Ensemble_score >= 0.92 + rule_match ("prompt_injection_high") => mark as Severity-1
- Ensemble_score between 0.7-0.92 with sustained repeats (>=5 distinct sessions / 10m) => Severity-2
- Alerts are weighted by customer-configured policies; Dedicated customers can tune thresholds and receive raw signal streams.

3) Detection-to-alert latency: our runtime maintains contiguous KV caches and incremental scoring. For the hosted tier we measure event generation at the model inference layer and pipeline to alerting. Typical numbers (p95/p99) provided earlier are measured end-to-end from model inference to alert push. For high-throughput dedicated pools we have observed p95 ~= 9s and p99 ~= 25s under provisioned capacity.

4) Sampling & retention:
- Default telemetry retention: 30 days of full fidelity, 365 days of aggregated metrics.
- SOC 2 customers can opt for 90-day full-fidelity retention; we can export raw telemetry to customer-managed buckets on request.
- PII/anonymization: we hash identifiers at ingestion and strip full prompts from low-risk events; high-risk events keep redacted snippets for triage.

5) Escalation matrix notes: automated priority escalation uses both route (region, capacity) and severity. The PDF includes the names and on-call rotation; we support email + PagerDuty + webhook notifications.

If useful, I can export a short runbook that shows a real incident reconstruction (redacted) and the alert timeline.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Applied Safety & Observability
Redwood Inference
Attachment references: telemetry snippets included in misuse_monitoring_evidence.csv

Marissa/Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Procurement confirms receipt and the security team will validate the samples tomorrow. A couple small follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm the exact SOC 2 audit report date and whether the log preservation configuration for SOC 2 customers is a billing-add or included in the Private deployment contract? We need this for our procurement checklist.
2) We noticed the retention_policy_summary.docx references the ability to export raw telemetry to S3; can you share the typical transfer cadence (near real-time, hourly batch) and whether exports include the full prompt text for flagged events?

If you can provide concise answers to those two points today, we'll be able to move the security review to legal. Also please add a single point-of-contact for post-signature integration (name, role, pager).

Appreciate the help — looking forward to closing this out.

Alex
Head of Platform Security
SafeHarbor Bank
